---
title: "Connect your REDCap project"
description: "Check, set up and use a live REDCap project."
---

You need two things from the project's **API** page in REDCap: the **API
URL** and an **API token**. Request a token there if you don't have one.

## REDCap user rights

| Right | Needed for |
|---|---|
| **API Export** | everything (required) |
| Data export access to the forms | reading those forms |
| **Logging** | incremental sync (otherwise each sync is a full download) |
| **API Import** | write-back, randomisation arm write-back, DRW module |
| Data Resolution Workflow: *Open, close and respond* | the [DRW module](drw-module.html) |
| Record Locking | locking forms in REDCap through the module |

A dedicated service account is best: it keeps one person's leave or role
change from breaking the connection.

## 1. Check the connection

The check is read-only:

```r
library(REDCapCDMSTAT)
redcap_check("https://redcap.your-institution.org/api/", token = "<your token>")
```

```
REDCap connection check: https://redcap.your-institution.org/api/

  PASS  API URL                            https://redcap.your-institution.org/api/
  PASS  Token format                       32 hexadecimal characters
  PASS  Server and token                   REDCap 14.5.2
  INFO  Project                            PID 1234: My trial (Development, longitudinal, repeating instruments)
  PASS  Data dictionary                    86 fields on 9 forms
  PASS  Record export                      412 records readable
  PASS  Logging export (incremental sync)  Allowed: syncs download only changed records
  INFO  CDMSTAT DRW External Module        Not installed or not enabled in this project (optional ...)
  INFO  Write-back                         Needs the API Import right; ...

Connection works.
```

| Result | What to do |
|---|---|
| *The server could not be reached* | Check the URL, VPN and firewall, and whether API access is allowed from this machine |
| *REDCap refused the token* | Copy the whole token; check it belongs to this project and server, and that the user has API Export |
| *No records readable* | The project is empty, or data access groups or export rights restrict the user |
| *Logging export not allowed* | Grant the Logging right, or accept full downloads |
| *Production project* | Test write-back, DRW sync and locking on a copy first |

## 2. Set it up

```r
nx <- cdmstat_setup("https://redcap.your-institution.org/api/")   # prompts for the token (hidden)
```

`cdmstat_setup()`:

1. **Re-runs the check** and stops if anything fails.
2. **Stores the token where you choose** (`store =`): your user `.Renviron`
   (`"renviron"`, the default), the OS keyring (`"keyring"`, needs the
   keyring package), or this R session only (`"session"`).
3. **Saves the connection**: the URL goes in `connection.json` in the data
   folder. The token is never written there, nor to the cache, ledger or
   generated scripts.
4. **Downloads the data** and returns the engine.

After setup, `run_app()`, `run_api()` and the web app connect to the project
automatically. You can do the same from the Shiny app's **Connection** tab:

<img src="../reference/figures/screenshots/shiny-connection.png" class="screenshot" alt="Connection tab">

## 3. Day-to-day

```r
nx <- cdmstat_from_env()    # or just run_app()
nx$sync()                   # incremental
nx$validate(); nx$raise_queries()
```

For near-real-time updates, point REDCap's **Data Entry Trigger** at the web
gateway (see [Web app](web-app.html#redcap-data-entry-trigger)).

## Other ways to connect

```r
# Explicit, e.g. in a scheduled script: token from an environment variable or keyring
nx <- cdmstat_connect("https://redcap.your-institution.org/api/", token_env = "REDCAP_API_TOKEN")
nx <- cdmstat_connect("https://redcap.your-institution.org/api/", keyring_service = "redcap_pid_1234")

# Environment variables for servers (see deploy/cdmstat.env.example)
# CDMSTAT_SOURCE=redcap  CDMSTAT_URL=...  CDMSTAT_TOKEN_ENV=REDCAP_API_TOKEN  CDMSTAT_DIR=/var/lib/cdmstat/project

cdmstat_disconnect()        # forget the saved connection (cache and ledger are kept)
```

## Security notes

- **Keep the token out of shared places.** Never put it in code, chat or
  email. If it has been exposed, regenerate it on the project's API page.
- **The cache holds identifiable data.** Keep the data folder on encrypted
  storage with access limited to the people who need it.
